stories.title: The Global Story: How North Korea pulled off a $6bn heist
stories.take: How they did it: fake recruiters on a real job site interviewed a Binance developer, sent a malware 'software test' as the final step, got a foothold, then used Binance's own internal AI to find and move the money • About $6.3B in crypto left in under 20 minutes for most of it; ~$3B was frozen by Tether and other central issuers, the rest scattered across ~12,000 wallets • The FBI blamed North Korea (wallets matched earlier campaigns); the arc runs Sony 2015 → Bangladesh Bank → Bybit $1.5B → Binance, with amounts doubling roughly every two years • US estimate: about half of North Korea's missile program is funded by hacking

stories.title: Piers closed from high surf, The Pantry reopens, Walk 16 miles across LA — Sunday Edition
stories.take: High surf closed the Ventura, Manhattan and Hermosa piers — waves up to 12 feet in Manhattan Beach, advisory until 3 p.m. Tuesday • LAX is recovering from Friday's ground stop: 60+ cancellations and 100 delays, down from nearly 280 cancellations Saturday, normal expected by tonight • The Original Pantry Cafe reopens Thursday Nov 19 under homelessness nonprofit Hope the Mission — 13 of 21 original staff back, credit cards finally accepted, 100% of profits to ending homelessness • The 21st Great Los Angeles Walk is Saturday Nov 21: 16+ miles from Echo Park to the ocean, about 600 walkers, Route 66 theme
